evidence: # Group relays by x for faster lookup" and the subsequent "Backtracking" over those groups
affordance_in_statement: You are designing a communication array and must select exactly k relay configurations ... each integer is between 1 and k inclusive ... for any two distinct chosen relays ... x1 != x2
secondary_shortcut_name: two-bitmask backtracking over y and z
removal_suggestion: This reduction follows mathematically from the immutable bounds, exact cardinality, and pairwise x-distinctness, so it cannot be removed by ordinary rewording. If presentation must be changed, describe the coordinates as opaque catalog attributes whose relationship to the required k relay slots is supplied indirectly by the scenario, rather than explicitly exposing that there are exactly k possible x-values.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Partitions candidates by x and searches for exactly one candidate from each x-group, tracking only used y and z values.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: each integer is between 1 and k inclusive; select exactly k; chosen relays must have pairwise distinct x, y, and z values

common_affordance: Because there are exactly k possible x-values, selecting k relays with pairwise distinct x-values is equivalent to selecting one relay from every x-group.

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: Used a general exact-cover Dancing Links search, which incurred excessive search overhead and timed out on the worst cases.
Enumerated every k-subset of the t relays with combinations, producing an intractable O(t choose k) search.
Built a large incompatibility graph and attempted an exponential clique-style search, which timed out for dense instances.

recommended_edit: Do not change the task semantics; instead, re-present the coordinate domain indirectly in the scenario so that the one-per-x-group equivalence is not explicitly signposted. For example, describe x as an opaque relay-slot label generated from a hidden catalog mapping, while retaining the same numeric input values and validity conditions.
regression_risk: Such a presentation-only change is unlikely to rescue the already-defeated brute-force and general exact-cover implementations, but it may not defeat a solver that derives the one-per-x reduction directly from the unchanged mathematics.
